title: Marge's closed esophagus and the operation
summary: Through Dick Kennedy they got Dr. MacDonald for Marge, whose esophagus had completely closed from nervous tension that began in Europe; an operation at St. Clare's saved her.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Dick Kennedy he was the one recommended that same doctor for Marge. When Marge was so sick. And he said, Zutto, there's nothing like getting a doctor that you know. He say, and Doctor — I forget his name just that quick.
MacDonald.

Yes. Doctor MacDonald, and he says, nothing like knowing a doctor he say. And Doctor MacDonald knows you. He comes into Ryan's all the time and everything. He says, so you get him to look after Marge. And that's when Marge was suffering
with that esophagus.
Oh yes?
Her esophagus had closed completely up.
Oh really?
Yes. And we went to another doctor that was giving Marge big pills to swallow and Marge couldn't get it down.
I couldn't even swallow one of them.

Yes, couldn't even swallow one. And all she wanted was sherbert and pizze Pete (Stearn) came to New York and he got us some sherbert. Pete (Stearn) he's a kid out of Chicago. And he found some sherbert at one of the big hotels he was living at.
Well she wanted something that would sort of soothe her pipes more or less?
Yes, that's right, that's right.
Because I couldn't retain even water.
Is that so?
When we came back from Europe, it started in Europe.
Well what was that then?
Nervous tension.
Oh, it was not sort of inflamed or anything?
No, they thought it was cancer at first.
Yes, I bet they did.

And this doctor that we were going to had taken exrays. I had had the GI series and all of that. And so after Dick Kennedy told Zutty to take me over to Doctor MacDonald. Doctor MacDonald told Zutty he would have to call this doctor and tell him he was letting him go you know for the ethics of medicine. couldn't just take me away from another doctor and also to get the xrays. And when Zutty brought the xrays to him and he looked at them he went out of the room and he came back and told Zutty and said, I have a bed reserved for Marge at the St. Clate's Hospital for Saturday. He said, her esophagus is completely closed. So I thought I was a
goner, I only weighed about 90 pounds. I had all, all the symptoms of cancer. Went in there and they opened my esophagus and I've been well ever since.
And he told Marge that she wouldn't be able to eat anything but baby food. And Marge has been rattling with chittlings.

Everything. And he was so proud of that operation he called me about six months later and asked me if I would come down to St. Clare's and let these other doctors talk to me. Now he said, you don't have to come because you're not a clinic patient. But you would be doing me a big favor. I said, you saved my life I'll do anything you tell me to do.
That's right, that's right.
And boy he had about a hundred doctors down there talking to me and looking at the exrays.
Well what had actually happened to the esophagus then?
It had completely closed. I had spasms at first.
The doctor told me that you couldn't even get a string of hair.
Well, why had it closed?
From nervous tension.
Really?
From nervous tension. That's all that caused it. Just getting so nervous and keeping it in you know and travels and worrying about bringing everything with us. And worrying about Zutty.
